It marks the end of a very short road for OpenAI's Mac-exclusive web browser, ChatGPT Atlas. OpenAI has shared details following the discontinuation of ChatGPT Atlas this weekend.

ChatGPT to replace ChatGPT Atlas as the new focus

As we reported in July, OpenAI is shutting down its standalone Atlas browser and instead integrating browser tools into a brand-new ChatGPT desktop application. After a brief transition period, Atlas is scheduled to stop functioning on August 9.

OpenAI warns that after that date, Atlas may no longer be able to open, browse, or run agentic workflows. Because the discontinued browser will no longer receive security updates, users should switch to other supported alternatives as soon as possible.

The transition may require some manual cleanup for some users. Atlas bookmarks will not transfer automatically. OpenAI advises users to export their bookmarks as HTML files and save important pages before the Sunday deadline.

Cookies may optionally be exported where feasible. ChatGPT conversation history is stored separately and will remain accessible.

Alternative AI browser options

OpenAI is directing users to the new ChatGPT desktop application. Its built-in browser supports multiple tabs, downloads, website logins, autofill, password management, extensions, and persistent browser state. However, this is not a browser-first experience.

When work requires using an existing Chrome profile, logged-in sessions, open tabs, or other extensions, the company recommends using its Chrome extension. The ChatGPT desktop app also includes a "computer use" feature that can selectively control Safari when granted permission.

On Mac, there are many other AI browser options, including Comet, Dia, Opera Neon, and Aside. Anthropic is pursuing a similar dual-track strategy: Claude Code offers a sandboxed in-app browser, while its Chrome extension works with existing logged-in sessions.
